name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Open seat with no incumbent penalty or advantage
Republican candidate has far outraised the Democrat
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 95%
model.rationale: The R+19 lean and a favorable 2026 environment make this open seat a heavy Republican favorite, and Chris Stigall's fundraising edge over Josh Smead reinforces that. Markets price a Republican win around 95%, consistent with a Safe R call.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or a Republican primary runoff hangover could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's sixth district is deeply Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly nineteen points to the right. Sam Graves's retirement creates an open seat, but the fundamentals still point strongly toward the GOP. Chris Stigall has raised about $600,000 and holds a cash advantage, while Democrat Josh Smead has raised under $75,000 with minimal cash on hand and no outside support on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which price a Republican win near 95 percent. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but is not a factor. The race is rated Safe Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
